security_claim: The verification failures in MIG-DELTA and INCIDENT-7 are caused not by quantum noise or circuit construction, but by an application-layer trust-boundary violation in ChallengeService.execute, which passes untrusted manifest compatibility_map permutations into compatibility_decode() prior to the authorization check; enforcing canonical q0..q(n-1) decoding (secure_decode / secure_decision) restores 100% soundness and completeness across all permutations.
root_cause_layer: Application post-processing / reporting adapter layer (compatibility_decode in ChallengeService.execute)

claims.claim: The fault is NOT quantum noise
claims.evidence: Phase A & B (results, localization_evidence): Raw backend counts are 100% deterministic (512/512 shots on a single bitstring, e.g. {'0101': 512} for MIG-DELTA) and match measurement-free Statevector probabilities (p = 1.0).
claims.assumption: The backend simulator (BasicSimulator) executes ideal unitary gates without decoherence or readout errors.
claims.limitation: On real NISQ quantum hardware, gate and readout noise will distribute shots across multiple keys, requiring a statistical threshold around dominant_key(counts).

claims.claim: The circuit DOES encode the registry value
claims.evidence: Phase B (circuit.draw, Statevector, canonical_bits_from_counts): Inspecting the Bernstein-Vazirani CX gates and reversing Qiskit's little-endian key yields '1010' for MIG-DELTA and '1100' for INCIDENT-7, matching registry_fingerprint.
claims.assumption: Qubit index i maps to canonical logical slot i (q0..q3) and build_bv_probe is not tampered with prior to compilation.
claims.limitation: Verifies that the prepared quantum oracle matches the registry in the demo cases, but cannot detect if an external actor replaces the quantum circuit itself with a matching spoofed oracle.

claims.claim: Metadata CAN alter the legacy decision (and CANNOT alter secure_decision)
claims.evidence: Phase B, C & E (controlled_experiment, minimal_reproducer, attack_demo): Holding the circuit constant ('1000' or '1010') while changing compatibility_map from [0, 1, 2, 3] to [1, 0, 2, 3] changes reported_fingerprint and flips MATCH to MISMATCH.
claims.assumption: The legacy service uses compatibility_decode(counts, compatibility_map) on untrusted manifest metadata before comparing against registry_fingerprint.
claims.limitation: Hamming weight invariant: because compatibility_map only permutes bit positions, metadata manipulation can only reach target strings with the exact same number of 0s and 1s.

claims.evidence: Phase D & Research Extension (defense_results, extension_results): secure_decode and secure_decision pass all unseen positive/negative tests, all 16x24 4-bit permutations, n-bit scaling (n=16), and blind metamorphic invariance tests.
claims.assumption: Registry fingerprints are defined in canonical q0..q(n-1) order and raw measurement counts originate from genuine quantum probe execution.
claims.limitation: Secures the classical decoding boundary against metadata tampering, but does not protect against an attacker who compromises the classical memory to overwrite raw counts or registry_fingerprint directly.
